Describe the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles.

say.en: A pancreas cell makes enzymes and ships them out of the cell. Who makes them, who packs them and who sends them out? In this lesson: Name the members of the endomembrane system.
Contrast RER and SER.
Describe the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles.

body.en: The endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles work in a coordinated way and form the endomembrane system. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it because their functions are not coordinated with these. The ER divides the cytoplasm into the luminal and extra-luminal compartments. Rough ER (with ribosomes) is active in protein synthesis and secretion; smooth ER is the major site of lipid synthesis, including steroidal hormones in animal cells. Camillo Golgi (1898) first saw the *Golgi apparatus*: flat cisternae with a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face. It packages materials and is the site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

points.en: Proteins from the ER are modified in the *Golgi* cisternae before release from its trans face.
The cis and trans faces are entirely different but interconnected.

say.en: The rough ER has ribosomes and makes proteins; the smooth ER makes lipids, including steroid hormones in animal cells.
Vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi. The proteins are modified and leave from the trans face.
From the trans face, vesicles go three ways: they become lysosomes, release secretions, or add to the plasma membrane.
Lysosomes are full of hydrolytic enzymes that work best at acidic pH. The vacuole is bounded by the tonoplast.

steps.en: Made on ribosomes attached to the rough ER
Enters the lumen of the rough ER
Carried in a transport vesicle to the cis (forming) face of the Golgi
Modified inside the Golgi cisternae (for example, glycoproteins formed)
Leaves from the trans (maturing) face in a secretory vesicle
Vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane and releases the protein

explanation.en: The ER, Golgi, lysosomes and vacuoles work together as the endomembrane system. Proteins made on the RER are packaged and modified in the Golgi before being sent out of the cell.

say.en: Follow one protein from where it is made to where it leaves the cell.

body.en: *Lysosomes* are membrane-bound vesicles formed by packaging in the Golgi. They are rich in hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at acidic pH and can digest carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids. The vacuole is bounded by a single membrane, the tonoplast, and holds water, sap, excretory products and materials not useful to the cell. In plant cells it can occupy up to 90% of the cell volume; the tonoplast moves ions into the vacuole against the gradient, so their concentration is much higher inside. Amoeba has a contractile vacuole for osmoregulation and excretion; many protists have food vacuoles.

points.en: Lysosome enzymes work best at acidic pH.
Tonoplast: the membrane of the vacuole.

problem.en: Trace the path of a digestive enzyme made by a pancreatic cell from its synthesis to its secretion.

steps.en: Ribosomes on the rough ER make the enzyme protein, which enters the ER lumen.
Vesicles carry it to the cis face of the Golgi, where it is modified and packaged.
Secretory vesicles leave the trans face and release the enzyme outside the cell.

answer.en: RER → Golgi (cis to trans) → secretory vesicles → outside
